scenarios.title: PAS $submit against the HL7 Da Vinci burden-reduction payer RI
scenarios.description: CHO's harness submits a synthetic PAS request bundle to the independent payer RI's Claim/$submit and parses/validates the PAS response bundle with the same FHIR parser CHO uses.

scenarios.title: CRD CDS Hooks exchange with the HL7 Da Vinci burden-reduction payer RI
scenarios.description: CHO acts as the provider-side CRD client: it discovers the payer RI's CDS Hooks services, selects the order-sign CRD service from discovery, invokes it with synthetic draft orders, and validates the CDS Hooks response and the Da Vinci coverage-information determinations it carries.

scenarios.title: DTR $questionnaire-package chained from the payer's own CRD determination
scenarios.description: CHO acts as the provider-side DTR client: it enters from the payer's own CRD determination, takes the DTR questionnaire canonical the payer named, requests exactly that canonical from the payer's $questionnaire-package, and validates the returned package and its declared dependencies.

scenarios.title: PAS $inquire against the burden-reduction payer RI
scenarios.description: Inquire on a prior authorization previously established by BR-PAS-SUBMIT-001 and validate the returned Parameters/responseBundle set.

scenarios.title: Inferno DTR payer-server suite against CHO
scenarios.description: Run the davinci-dtr-test-kit dtr_payer_server suite with CHO's FHIR base as the suite input and map Inferno result statuses into InteropResult.

scenarios.title: Inferno PDex payer-server suite against CHO
scenarios.description: Run the davinci-pdex-test-kit pdex_payer_server suite with CHO's FHIR base as the suite input.

scenarios.title: Inferno PDex payer-client suite driven by CHO
scenarios.description: Run the davinci-pdex-test-kit pdex_payer_client suite with CHO acting as the payer client performing $member-match and clinical data retrieval.

findings.summary: The payer advertises 6 CRD service(s): appointment-book-crd[appointment-book], encounter-discharge-crd[encounter-discharge], encounter-start-crd[encounter-start], order-dispatch-crd[order-dispatch], order-select-crd[order-select], order-sign-crd[order-sign]. Selected 'order-sign-crd' for hook 'order-sign' by hook match, not list position.
Service 'order-sign-crd' advertises prefetch keys: coverage, deviceHistory, encounter, medicationHistory, patient, practitioner, practitionerRoles, questionnaireResponses, serviceHistory.
Billing code L8000 -> covered=covered, pa-needed=auth-needed, doc-needed=no-doc, questionnaire=present, billingCode=L8000.
The payer named a DTR questionnaire alongside its prior-authorization determination, which is the CRD-to-DTR hand-off a later scenario can follow.

Three billing codes produced three distinct determinations — L8000: covered=covered, pa-needed=auth-needed, doc-needed=no-doc, questionnaire=present, billingCode=L8000; J3490: covered=not-covered, billingCode=J3490; E0100: covered=conditional, info-needed=detail-code.
CHO advertises CRD hooks [order-select, order-sign]; the payer advertises [appointment-book, encounter-discharge, encounter-start, order-dispatch, order-select, order-sign].

CHO and the payer use different service ids for hook 'order-select'. Service ids are server-chosen and clients resolve them from discovery, so this is expected rather than a defect — recorded because a client that hard-coded an id would break on it.

CHO's CDS Hooks discovery does not advertise a davinci-crd.version extension, which the payer does. A CRD client cannot tell from CHO's discovery which CRD version CHO implements. Recorded as an observation for follow-up, not adjudicated here.
Resolved CRD service 'order-sign-crd' for hook 'order-sign' from discovery, by hook match rather than a hard-coded id.

CRD (L8000) named http://example.org/fhir/Questionnaire/PriorAuthRequired; $questionnaire-package returned resources: Questionnaire=1, QuestionnaireResponse=1; questionnaires: http://example.org/fhir/Questionnaire/PriorAuthRequired; outcome issues: 1

http://example.org/fhir/Questionnaire/PriorAuthRequired declares no Library, ValueSet or sub-questionnaire dependencies, so the package is complete without them. Recorded so a future upstream change that adds a dependency is visible as a change rather than passing silently.

The payer reported alongside the package for L8000: Warning/Informational: Patient demographic pre-population skipped: no Patient in this payer's records matched Coverage.beneficiary.identifier or Coverage.subscriberId (sender-supplied reference 'Patient/interop-member-001' is not trusted as a lookup key to avoid PHI leakage on id collision). Supply Coverage.subscriberId or Coverage.beneficiary.identifier matching a payer member identifier.

CRD (E0466) named http://example.org/fhir/Questionnaire/DocumentationRequired; $questionnaire-package returned resources: Questionnaire=1, QuestionnaireResponse=1; questionnaires: http://example.org/fhir/Questionnaire/DocumentationRequired; outcome issues: 1

http://example.org/fhir/Questionnaire/DocumentationRequired declares no Library, ValueSet or sub-questionnaire dependencies, so the package is complete without them. Recorded so a future upstream change that adds a dependency is visible as a change rather than passing silently.

The payer reported alongside the package for E0466: Warning/Informational: Patient demographic pre-population skipped: no Patient in this payer's records matched Coverage.beneficiary.identifier or Coverage.subscriberId (sender-supplied reference 'Patient/interop-member-001' is not trusted as a lookup key to avoid PHI leakage on id collision). Supply Coverage.subscriberId or Coverage.beneficiary.identifier matching a payer member identifier.
Billing code L8000 led to http://example.org/fhir/Questionnaire/PriorAuthRequired; E0466 led to http://example.org/fhir/Questionnaire/DocumentationRequired.

CHO and the payer RI advertise different OperationDefinition canonicals for Claim/$inquire. Recorded as an interoperability finding; which side matches the PAS IG is for the follow-up PR to establish against the published IG, not for the harness to assume.
The payer RI returned review action code(s) [A3] for the submitted synthetic item.

disclaimers: External interoperability evidence shows that Cloud Health Office exchanged standards-conformant requests and responses with an independently developed implementation it does not own. It is not CMS certification, ONC certification, or an HL7 endorsement.
Every exchange uses synthetic data against a pinned reference implementation. A pin represents the version tested, not every implementation of the same specification.
Protocol interoperability is not payer rule parity: two payers running different rule content can interoperate perfectly and still reach different coverage decisions.
